# drone-duel-wallclock-program-standard

| | |
|---|---|
| Benchmark | Embodied Agent Olympiad |
| Mode | standard (`eai-standard-realtime/1.0`) |
| Twin | — (standard only: Olympiad sports have no privileged twin) |
| Simulator / robot | `mujoco (CPU, 500 Hz rigid-body quadrotor with lagged rotors, linear drag in a seeded wind, kinematic shutters)` / `none` |
| Family / instance | `drone_duel` |
| Oracle | `full` — solution/: the sport's reference player (camera images and /spec only); tools/check runs it live and it wins the default configuration |
| Agent time budget | 7200 s; tokens: protocol default (PROTOCOL §5) |
| Base image | `ghcr.io/mll-lab-nu/eai-olympiad:0.1.0` |

## Task
Fly an original simulated quadrotor through a seeded course of numbered gates by its front camera and its own telemetry, commanding world-frame velocity and yaw rate; format racing: three qualifying rounds alone (level 1-3), format duel: heats against another player who flies the same level-2 course at the same time in a world of its own, the first to two heat wins wins; format `duel` (seats A, B),
action level `low`, program play. Generated by `tools/generate.py` from
`sports/drone/sport.toml`; do not edit by hand.

Deviations from the rulebook:

|---|---|---|

## Difficulty
Set at run time: the seed (`RO_SEED`; it draws the match's random conditions) and the first player (`FIRST_PLAYER`; play both orders).

## Reference solution
`solution/solve.sh` runs the sport's reference player (`solution/builtin_players.py`) through the core's client
(`solution/ro_client.py`): camera images and `/spec` only.

## Verification
The `sim` service (the v0.2 core, `environment/sim/core/`) records the match (`episode.jsonl`) and a fresh process
replays it (state hash); the verifier (`tests/grade.py` = `core/grading.py`, no network) writes the common reward
fields (`success`, `valid_trial`, `deterministic`, `<seat>_won`, ...) and the sport's fields (`tests/sport_grade.py`).

## Details
| | |
|---|---|
| Rules | [FAI Sporting Code Section 4 (Aeromodelling), Volume F9 Drone Sports, chapter C, class F9U Drone Racing](https://www.fai.org/sites/default/files/document/file/SC4_volume_CIAM_F9_Drone_sports_2026.pdf) version 2026 edition (effective 1 January 2026) |
| id | rule | deviation |
| D1 | C.2, C.6 | one flight through an open course (the C.2 'open loop to be flown once') per round or heat, not three laps of a closed circuit in 3 minutes; the time limit is 35 / 60 / 120 s for levels 1 / 2 / 3 |
| D2 | C.6.3 | format racing: exactly 3 qualifying rounds, Option 1 ranking (the best result; the 2nd and 3rd results split ties) with one lap; a round's result is its finish time, or the gates passed and the time at the last gate when it did not finish (gates as the sectors C.2 allows) |
| D3 | C.6.4, C.6.5 | format duel: a race of two pilots instead of four, flown as successive final races (C.6.5.3): the first to win two heats wins; a tied heat is re-flown, at most 5 heats; then more heat wins, the C.6.3 a order (best, second best, ... heat result), the winner of the last heat that had one, and a seeded lot |
| D4 | C.6.4 | a heat ends as soon as its placing is decided (the other drone is down or home and cannot catch up) |
| D5 | C.2, C.6.2 | both drones start at the same point, each in a world of its own (no mid-air collision, no restarts for collisions, C.8.2), and neither sees the other |
| D6 | C.6.1, C.6.2 | the clock starts when the world runs (after game start / game ready), with no start tone and no false start; qualifying rounds are timed from the start, not from a timing gate |
| D7 | C.7.2 | a gate counts only when the drone's centre crosses its plane forwards at least 0.18 m inside every edge (the whole drone through the opening); a missed gate may be flown again |
| D8 | C.7.3, C.9.1 | any contact (gate, panel, shutter, floor, wall) ends the flight; leaving the arena (the safety line) ends it as in C.9.1 |
| D9 | C.2 | added: moving shutters (levels 2, 3), wind (levels 2, 3) and floor-to-ceiling panels to fly round (level 3); the course is fixed by the seed, the wind and the shutter phases change every round |
| D10 | C.1 | an original 0.35 kg simulated quadrotor commanded by world-frame velocity and yaw rate through an onboard attitude controller, not an FPV pilot's stick inputs; FPV image 320 x 240; exact own-state telemetry |
